newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs to compensate Communist-era prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Czechs to compensate Communist-era prisoners.

text.p: The Czech cabinet agreed on Wednesday to make one-off compensation payments to political prisoners of former Communist governments, taking another step to settle accounts with the country's totalitarian past.

Health Minister Jan Strasky told a news conference that the government voted to pay a total of around 400 million crowns ($12.6 million) to the victims of political persecution who were jailed in prisons and labour camps.
"The government will pay out a one-off reimbursement to the victims," Strasky said.

Each political prisoner would get 625 crowns for every month spent in a Communist jail between February 1948, when the Communists seized power in Prague, and November 1989, the month of Prague's non-violent "Velvet Revolution", he said.
The minister did not say how many people were expected to claim the payment, or if families of deceased former prisoners would be eligible.
Thousands were believed to have been imprisoned during four decades of Communist political purges.
Among measures taken after the revolution to come to terms with the Soviet-era dictatorship, the Czechs banned former secret police agents from taking high-ranking civil service functions.
The parliament also last year approved allowing individuals to see their own secret police files which may reveal, for some, the idenity of previously unknown informants or collaborators.
But only a few representatives of the communist government have been jailed for human rights violations and other offences. ($ = 31.79 Czech Crowns)
